items.function: onboard pack switch MOSFETs; external pack switch module; pack overvoltage and transient clamp
items.requirement: Round 1 refutes IPT015N10N5ATMA1 and the VS-FC420SA10 and VS-FC270SA20 modules on safe operating area during the controlled turn-off. It finds no clamp that holds the pack node under 85 V at up to 600 A. Answered under Raised by P1: V270: 0 to 50 °C ambient. Supply: the ESC pack from its lowest voltage (V181) to 67.2 V, 16 cells at 4.2 V (F15); the gate drive from the 3.2 to 3.4 V logic window; the clamp holds the pack node under 85 V. The same range answers V38's question for the safety gate and the ESC pack switches (owner, 2026-10-01) V324: The bus capacitance with damping, with no clamp part. It is a stage 2 requirement for the 300 A onboard path, from FU-2A's figures: 6 x 330 µF at 35 to 52 mOhm, a peak under 82 V, 45 mJ at 1 µH, the loop inductance stated as assumed. The 600 A external path and the external pack switch module are not known. A pass-2 run of R3 researches the switched-node freewheel diode (owner, 2026-10-03)
items.source: hardware/STATUS.md, ESC pack switch; Control.md, Not known
items.reason: requirement changed after round 1 or round 1 left the function without a part (Research.md, Round 2, Follow-ups)

items.requirement: An isoSPI (isolated SPI) transceiver pair or a digital isolator between the ADBMS1818ASWAZ-RL and the measurement coprocessor's SPI1, rated 85 V DC working or more (V189). Answered under Raised by P1: V289: A digital isolator on direct SPI, rated 85 V DC working or more (V189). Its current is for research (owner, 2026-10-01). Its pack side runs from an always-on supply referenced to the pack negative, not from the ADBMS1818's regulator, which is off while the monitor sleeps; the same supply gives the ADBMS1818 an external VREG, and V+ of 16 V or more for packs under 16 V. That supply is a function of R9 (owner, 2026-10-02)
items.source: V189; IOBoard.md, Cell monitor isolation; Pins.md
items.reason: requirement changed after round 1 or round 1 left the function without a part (Research.md, Round 2, Follow-ups)

items.function: switched-node freewheel diode (negative clamp of the ESC-side node, V54)
items.requirement: No part: FU-2A's P3 named it a missed function and the re-rank returned no candidate. The diode clamps the ESC-side switched node when the pack switch opens (V54). It carries 300 A onboard and 600 A external for the 0.5 uH discharge, 22.5 mJ and 90 mJ, and stands 67.2 V reverse with the switch closed (F15). The turn-off qualification of IPT015N10N5ATMA1 assumes about 1 V across it, VDS up to 86 V with the node under 85 V. Read its forward voltage at 300 A, its single-pulse current and energy ratings and its reverse rating, and state the onboard turn-off margin with it. The 600 A external path is not known (V324): state the diode's figures there as reported, not as pass or fail. The ESC pack node is held by its bus capacitance with damping, a stage 2 requirement, not a clamp part (V324)
items.source: FU-2A/016-P3-R3.json missed functions; FU-2A/012-P2-R3.json 'onboard switch turn-off'; V54, V270, V324

items.function: onboard pack switch driver; external module driver output
items.requirement: The drivers take the latch output alone; no coprocessor signal reaches them (V53). A motor overcurrent or over-temperature opens the ESC pack switches through the coprocessor's failsafe latch and the panel's heartbeat: the latched coprocessor refuses the panel's control writes, the panel stops its heartbeat, and the monostable opens the switches, within the 500 ms stop deadline (V159, V160)
items.source: V53, V159, V160, V288; IOBoard.md, Not defeatable

items.requirement: Feeds the ADBMS1818's V+ from each balance-lead tap that can be the pack top, so V+ stays at or above C18 - 0.3 V and C18 at or under V+ + 5.5 V for 1 to 16 cells up to 67.2 V, with no cell-count setting (V193, V327). With only the LTM8068EY#PBF's fixed 18 V on V+, V+ falls below C18 - 0.3 V above 18.0 V of pack, and C18 exceeds V+ + 5.5 V above 23.2 V. Requirements (V327, FU-2D): the pack-side branch drops at most 0.3 V at 1.4 mA, the ADBMS1818's highest V+ current; the supply-side branch blocks up to 67.2 V less the supply voltage, and the pack-side branch blocks the supply into the pack; both rated with V188's 85 V in mind; with the board off, V+ draws 6.1 uA typical and 18 uA maximum from the pack top through it, a draw V190 does not count. State the placements a board and the stock gate at that count

found_values.value: Barrier pack-side current, at VCC2 = 5 V from the always-on pack-side supply (not from VREG, owner 2026-10-02). Rank 1 ISO7741DWR ICC2: 2.8 typ / 4.6 mA max at 1 Mbps and 4.2 / 6.4 mA max at 10 Mbps, all channels switching, CL 15 pF; DC 2.0 / 3.7 mA max with inputs high and 3.2 / 5.2 mA max with inputs low. The 1 MHz SPI clock is 2 Mbps, between the tabulated rates, so 6.4 mA bounds it; the idle monitor (CS and SCK high, SPI mode 3) draws 3.7 to 5.2 mA. The tables give VCC1 = VCC2 = 5 V; a 3.3 V host side with a 5 V pack side is not tabulated. Rank 2 ISO6741DWR: 4.5 mA max at 1 Mbps, 6.5 mA max at 10 Mbps, DC 3.5 / 5.1 mA max. Rank 3 ISOW7741BDFMR takes its pack side from its own converter (IISOIN, FU-2D: 8.9 mA max at 10 Mbps)

requirements.name: separate input

requirements.name: one connector
requirements.value: 16 cells on one 17-pin connector; each pack's leads arrive through an adapter lead

requirements.name: no count setting

requirements.name: pack-side interface

requirements.name: V+ from the supply

found_values.value: set: the latch powers up with the gates disabled and only the operator clear control enables them; the latch reset (MR) is tied to the enable node, which the reset supervisor and the 100 kOhm pull-down hold low through the 3.3 V ramp
found_values.source: STATUS.md:340 ('Every stop latches; nothing re-arms on its own.'); F11 Answer (Research.md, Blocking); IOBoard.md, Link and safety, Latch and Power-up rows; checkout 7e74cd442a79

found_values.value: between the enable node and the gates: the latch output drives the output buffer enable, the servo rail gate drivers, both ESC pack switch drivers and, through the inverter, the external CAN transceiver standby; the enable node keeps the monostable's own timing, which test steps 7 and 10 read
found_values.source: Monostable.md@23c82ca:395-410 (Power path), :420-437 (Fail-safe direction); IOBoard.md, Link and safety, Latch row; V326 Answer

found_values.value: a momentary normally-open push button on the IO board, wired to the latch clock through a resistor-capacitor debounce and a Schmitt buffer (the latch clock Schmitt buffer), with no processor, register or firmware between contact and latch
found_values.source: F11 Answer (Research.md, Blocking); Monostable.md@23c82ca:451-455 (Not defeatable); IOBoard.md, Link and safety, Not known (clear control line)

found_values.value: relay: no; firmware on either board: no. F11 clears the latch only by an operator action, and no processor, register or firmware sits in the path from GPIO6 to either gate
found_values.source: F11 question and Answer (Research.md, Blocking); Monostable.md@23c82ca:451-455; IOBoard.md, Link and safety, Not defeatable row

found_values.value: yes: the high-side switch on each servo rail is the servo rail gate, one on each of the 3 servo rails and one on the adjustable supply's output, 4 a board; the 20 port supply switches, driven through the I/O expander, are not a gate
found_values.source: IOBoard.md, Link and safety, Servo rail gate row and Not known (owner, 2026-09-30); Monostable.md@23c82ca:451-455 (Not defeatable)

found_values.value: at least 85 V, 17.8 V above the 67.2 V of F15: the open switch holds the pack node, which stays under the INA228's 85 V (V270, V324); a 100 V part leaves 32.8 V above 67.2 V and passes, an 80 V part (12.8 V) does not
found_values.source: INA228 datasheet SLYS021A, section 6.1 (common-mode and VBUS -0.3 V to 85 V), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina228.pdf; F15 Answer; V270 and V324 Answers

found_values.value: 300 A: V50's peak of 300 A for 30 s at most; 'and more' carries no figure. The external path and its module are not known (V324)
found_values.source: V50 and V324 Answers (Research.md, Raised by P1)

found_values.value: 0.57 uA at 50 degC for the 74HC423: its input leakage limit of +/-0.1 uA at 25 degC (VCC 6.0 V) doubled every 10 degC (0.1 x 2^2.5 = 0.566 uA); the same table limits it to +/-1.0 uA over -40 to 85 degC and gives no separate figure for the nREXT/CEXT pin
found_values.source: 74HC423 Rev. 8.1, Table 6 (II), https://assets.nexperia.com/documents/data-sheet/74HC423.pdf

found_values.value: under 5 mA a rail: the placeholder of pull request #167 is the idle current of the lightest load the rail carries; a micro servo, Savox SH-0255MG+, states a quiescent current of 5 mA
found_values.source: Monostable.md@23c82ca:411-416; Savox SH-0255MG+ product page, 'Quiescent Current (mA) 5', https://savox-servo.com/en/product/SH-0255MGplus/savox-servo-sh-0255mg-digital-dc-motor-metal-gear (vendors.py fetch, HTTP 200)

found_values.value: none: only switching transients are clamped, and the bus capacitance with damping holds the ESC pack node under 85 V (V324, a stage 2 requirement); the highest sustained input is the 67.2 V of a 16-cell pack at 4.2 V a cell
found_values.source: F15 Answer; V324 Answer; V41 question (Research.md, Raised by P1)

found_values.value: 125 ns: the 74HC423 nRD LOW pulse width minimum over -40 to 85 degC at VCC 2.0 V, the lowest supply its table states (25 ns at 4.5 V); the term the 3.3 V regulator ramp sets is P5's power-up check, which FU-2P56 found within (release at least 2.4 ms after regulation)
found_values.source: 74HC423 Rev. 8.1, Table 7 (tW, nRD input LOW), https://assets.nexperia.com/documents/data-sheet/74HC423.pdf; FU-2P56/002-P5.json budget 'power-up sequence'

found_values.value: at least 27 V: in operation the gate sees at most 18 V, the TPS55285 output overvoltage trip at 120 % of the 15 V top set point (its VOUT pin is rated 17 V absolute maximum); a converter whose switches fail short passes its input, which the bus clamp and capacitance hold at or under 27 V, the TPS55285 VIN absolute maximum (V318, V320)
found_values.source: TPS55285 SLVSI72A, sections 5.1 (VIN, SW1 -0.3 to 27 V; VOUT, SW2 -0.3 to 17 V) and 5.5 (VVOUT_OVP_FB 110.5 to 120 %), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps55285.pdf; V318, V319, V320 Answers

found_values.value: yes: an ESC with regenerative braking returns current to the pack through the closed switch; the tree states no figure, so the onboard path's 150 A continuous rating (F2) bounds it in either direction
found_values.source: shared/ui/programmer_screen.c:199-201 ('Regen braking ... Puts braking energy back into the pack rather than into the motor'); F2 Answer

found_values.value: 2.8 V: SET_PACK_CELLS takes 1 cell, and the lowest per-cell low-voltage cut the tree offers for an ESC is 2.8 V, so a 1-cell ESC pack can run down to 2.8 V
found_values.source: shared/settings/settings.c:39-41 (pack_cells 1 to 14); shared/ui/programmer_screen.c:139-141 and :202-204 ('Low voltage cut', 28 to 38, unit V, one decimal)

found_values.value: level: the latch sets on the enable node's low level (the enable node drives the latch's asynchronous reset), and set wins when set and clear are both active
found_values.source: STATUS.md:340 ('nothing re-arms on its own'); F11 question (Research.md, Blocking); 74LVC1G175 Rev. 11, function table (MR LOW forces Q LOW whatever CP)

report.value: The switch drivers take the latch output alone (V53). A motor overcurrent or over-temperature opens the switches through the coprocessor's failsafe latch: it refuses the panel's control writes, the panel stops its heartbeat, and the monostable opens the switches (V160), within the 500 ms stop deadline (V159). FU-2P56 bounds that path at about 277 ms (17 ms to the INA228 alert, 20 ms to the disarm, 50 ms panel poll, 185 ms of the monostable, 5 ms of the switch); the coprocessor's action is not built in its firmware (V160)

exclusions_not_holding.reason_given: Fail 'chip select idle high' (Pins.md:151-155): the F suffix defaults low on input power loss (SLLSEP4K section 4, SLLSFJ6G p. 1, SLLSFK1C section 5)
exclusions_not_holding.why_it_fails: Pins.md:151-155 (checkout 7e74cd442a79, read 2026-10-03) says only that every chip select has an external pull-up of about 10 kOhm and that RP2350 pads come out of reset pulled down (32 to 86 kOhm), which would select every chip while the coprocessor resets. In that state the host rail is up, the isolator input is high and an F part's output is high; the F suffix acts only when the input side loses power. No line of Pins.md, IOBoard.md or Research.md (checked by grep for 'unpowered', 'host side', 'host-side') states a host-side-unpowered case, so 'CS stays deasserted while the host side is unpowered' is P2's addition and not a requirement value. In that case an F part holds CSB, SCK and SDI at 0 V; with P2's own wake value (SCK - CSB at least 200 mV for 240 ns) the difference is 0 mV, so it does not wake the ADBMS1818. The drop stands only if the owner adds a host-unpowered requirement. At JLCPCB the F rows do not displace rank 1 or 2 (ISO7741FDWR 1.7509 at 1 and ISO6741FDWR 1.9167 at 1 per FU-2D, against 1.4745 for ISO7741DWR), so they are alternates, not new first choices.

The ADuM5410/ADuM5411/ADuM5412 data sheet answers HTTP 200 at https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/ADuM5410-5411-5412.pdf (vendors.py fetch --client safari, 922,072 bytes, Rev. B, read 2026-10-03T11:07:53Z); the underscore name answers 404. Read against P2's values: VDD1 (side 1 logic, 3.0 to 5.5 V) is independent of VDDP (converter input), so the ADuM5401 reason 'one supply sets the converter and the side-1 logic, VIH 0.7 x VDD1' does not apply to this family; 3 forward and 1 reverse, 150 Mbps, tPLH/tPHL 13 ns max (Table 5), VIH 0.7 x VDDx, VDD2 independent of VDDP (pin table). The part still does not qualify as P2's barrier and pack-side supply in one: data outputs default low (Table 32), VISO is 4.7 V min with load regulation 5 % max (Table 3), so 4.47 V at the data sheet's bound against the 4.5 V minimum, and IISO(MAX) is 30 mA against 16.5 + 8.1 mA + IDD2 6.85 mA max at 1 Mbps (Table 4) = 31.45 mA. JLCPCB stock 517 / 504 at 17.123 at 1 piece (vendors.py jlcpcb C2830727, 2026-10-03T11:07:44Z). As a barrier alone, with VDDP unused, it is a pricier alternate that defaults low, below ISO7741DWR.

missed_functions.why: IOBoard.md:475 names it as a required line: per cell voltage and resistance under load, and per pack capacity and drawn mAh. P2's 'Cell monitor' entry carries per-cell voltage and resistance under load from the INA228's motor current (its 'quantities' row) but nothing for the per-pack capacity and drawn mAh, and no entry or source of those two figures (the INA228's charge register is R8's, not named in R9). IOBoard.md:524 also names how cell samples align with the motor current for the per-cell resistance; P2 records that only as 'not fixed: V187 not found'.

report.value: The page states a chip select held high through a coprocessor reset (Pins.md:151-155: external pull-up of about 10 kOhm, pad pull-down 32 to 86 kOhm). With the host rail up, the input sits at 2.51 to 2.96 V, above the isolator's 2.31 V threshold (0.7 x 3.3 V), and an F part's output follows its input. The F default (low) acts only when the input side is unpowered or the input open. No line of Pins.md, IOBoard.md or Research.md states the host side unpowered while the pack side runs; P2's 'unpowered' wording is not in the cited lines. Four F rows qualify and rank below their default-high twins. data.function: P2 report: V+ OR element: no part
data.ruling: The refutation stands on the drop values. The figure says PMEG100T30ELP, PMEG10030ELP, PMEG10010ELR and PMEG100V060ELPD drop "about 0.33 to 0.4 V typical at 1 mA, 25 C". The PMEG100T30ELP's own 25 C curve gives about 0.27 V at 1 mA and about 0.28 V at 1.4 mA. That is under V327's 0.3 V at 1.4 mA. The PMEG10030ELP gives about 0.30 V at 1 mA. So the stated range is wrong, and the PMEG100T30ELP is the nearest candidate, not one of the parts that fail on drop at 25 C. The conclusion that no part is shown to meet both V327 and V190 still holds. Three reasons: the PMEG100T30ELP's interpolated 0 C drop is about 0.32 V typical, over 0.3 V at the cold end of V7's 0 to 50 C; its data sheet gives no forward-voltage maximum below 0.5 A; it gives no reverse current between 25 C and 85 C. The figure's value has to be corrected. Its "no part" outcome is unchanged. The scope is function: the fault is in this function's requirement check, not in any part's lifecycle, maker or LCSC identity.
data.evidence: The PMEG100T30ELP data sheet (Nexperia, 19 July 2024, 260,074 B) was rendered at 200 dpi and its Fig. 3 (forward current vs forward voltage, typical, pulsed) was pixel-scanned. The scale is 0 V at x=260 px and 0.4 V at x=408 px, which is 370 px per volt. At IF = 1 mA (bottom gridline), curve (6), Tj = 25 C, sits at x=361, which is 0.273 V. At 1.4 mA (y about 682) it sits at x about 362.5, which is 0.277 V. Curve (7), Tj = -40 C, gives 0.396 V at 1.4 mA. Linear interpolation to 0 C gives about 0.32 V. Table 7 gives VF maxima only from 0.5 A upward (550 mV maximum at 0.5 A, 25 C). It gives IR 0.1 uA typical and 0.8 uA maximum at 60 V, 25 C, then 0.42 mA typical at 100 V, 125 C. There is no IR figure at 50 C. The PMEG10030ELP data sheet (20 February 2023, 264,246 B), Fig. 4, curve (5) at 25 C, gives about 0.30 V at 1 mA by visual reading of the plot, about 0.31 V at 1.4 mA. Both readings disagree with the stated "about 0.33 to 0.4 V". The verifier's leakage figures were not re-read here: BAT46 at 35.6 uA and 39.6 uA summed, PMEG10010ELR at 150 nA maximum. They are not what the refutation contests. The PMEG10010ELR and PMEG100V060ELPD data sheets were fetched (HTTP 200, 291,987 B and 735,261 B) and their forward-voltage pages rendered (p. 6 and p. 7). Those curves were not scanned or read. Their drops (about 0.35 V and 0.32 V) rest on the verifier's reading only. The ruling rests on the PMEG100T30ELP reading alone.

data.function: P2 report: LTM8068 minimum load and preload
data.ruling: The refutation stands. P2's readings of the graphs are correct. The minimum load is about 15 mA at VOUT1 = 18 V, at 25 C. The maximum load at 18 V from VIN = 5 V is about 80 mA. 1.8 kOhm at 18 V draws 10 mA and dissipates 0.18 W. The conclusion that about 10 mA of preload keeps VOUT1 in regulation while the monitor sleeps does not hold. P2 sized the sleep load with the ISO7741's side-2 maximum, 5.2 mA, which applies only with the inputs low. A maximum is the wrong bound for a minimum-load check. While the ADBMS1818 sleeps, the SPI bus idles with CSB and SCK high (SPI mode 3) and SDO pulled up. In that state ICC2 is 2.0 mA typical and 3.7 mA maximum, so the module carries 12.0 to 13.7 mA, below 15 mA. Even the inputs-low case, at 3.2 mA typical, gives only 13.2 mA. The 15 mA figure is also a room-temperature typical. LTM8068 p. 14 says a colder application may need a larger minimum load and must be characterized at its lowest operating temperature. The preload must therefore be larger than 10 mA and sized against the barrier's smallest current at the lowest operating temperature. That value is not read. The awake budget leaves room for it: about 80 mA available against 32.4 mA without the preload. The ruling concerns how this function's preload is sized, not the LTM8068 or ISO7741 as parts.
data.evidence: LTM8068 Rev. D p. 6, graph 8068 G19 'Minimum Load Current vs VOUT1 Over Full Input Voltage Range' (TA = 25 C): the curve crosses 15 mA at VOUT1 = 18 V, rising from about 7 mA at 3 V to about 21 mA at 24 V. p. 5, graph 8068 G15 'Maximum Load Current vs VOUT1': VIN = 5 V at VOUT1 = 18 V is about 80 mA. p. 14, 'Minimum Load': 'Note that this graph describes room temperature operation. If the end application operates at a colder temperature, the minimum load requirement may be higher and the minimum load condition must be characterized for the lowest operating temperature.' ISO7741 SLLSEP4K (revised August 2026), table 5.10, Supply Current Characteristics, 5-V Supply, p. 14, ISO7741 'Supply current - DC signal', EN1 = EN2 = VCCI: with VI = VCCI, ICC2 is 2.0 mA typical and 3.7 mA maximum (ICC1 1.5 / 2.9). With VI = 0 V, ICC2 is 3.2 mA typical and 5.2 mA maximum (ICC1 4.8 / 6.8). The 3.3-V table 5.12 gives ICC2 2.0 / 3.7 and 3.2 / 5.1. ADBMS1818: the part 'supports SPI Mode 3 (CPHA = 1 and CPOL = 1)', and SDO is an open-drain output that needs a pull-up. Sums: 10 + 2.0 = 12.0 mA and 10 + 3.7 = 13.7 mA with the inputs high; 10 + 3.2 = 13.2 mA with the inputs low, typical; each is below 15 mA. 18 V / 1.8 kOhm = 10 mA; 18 V x 10 mA = 0.18 W.
data.source: https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/ltm8068.pdf (Rev. D; vendors.py fetch --client safari; pp. 5 and 6 rendered at 130 dpi and read as images, p. 14 text). https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/iso7741.pdf (SLLSEP4K; vendors.py fetch; tables 5.10 p. 14 and 5.12). data.function: P2 report: barrier pins for P5
data.ruling: The refutation stands. The four pin assignments in the figure are correct: GPIO 8 SPI1_RX, GPIO 10 SPI1_SCLK, GPIO 11 SPI1_TX, and GPIO 15 as the cell monitor CS (SIO, pulled up). The second clause fails. It says the isolator's enables are tied high and take no pin. The cited lines, Pins.md:105-112, say nothing about isolator enables. No other line of Pins.md or IOBoard.md at 7e74cd442a79 says it either. The datasheets also contradict it for the rank-1 barrier, ISO7741DWR. GPIO 8 is one SPI1_RX net shared by the ADS1235 (CS GPIO 9), the MAX31856 (CS GPIO 13) and, across the barrier, the ADBMS1818 (Pins.md:105, 156-158). The ISO7741's reverse channel output, OUTD (pin 6, side 1), drives a push-pull level whenever EN1 (pin 7) is high or open. Its input is the ADBMS1818 SDO. SDO is an open-drain output with a pull-up, and it goes high when CSB goes high. With EN1 tied high, OUTD therefore drives SPI1_RX high continuously. That fights the MISO output of the ADS1235 or MAX31856 whenever either is selected. To put OUTD in high impedance, EN1 must follow the cell monitor's chip select. EN1 is active high and CS is active low, so this needs an inverter from GPIO 15 or one more GPIO. Either way the figure P5 would budget (enables tied high, no part, no pin) is wrong. Scope is function: the defect concerns this barrier's connection to the shared SPI1 and the resources P5 budgets for it. It does not concern the ISO7741DWR's lifecycle, maker or LCSC identity. The verifier said no page states a tri-state requirement. That does not save the clause: the figure asserts a connection that the shared net in Pins.md and the ISO7741 datasheet show to be faulty.
data.evidence:
Pins.md (checkout 7e74cd442a79), read 2026-10-03T12:00Z:
- :105 "8 | SPI1_RX | measurement SPI RX (MISO); reaches the cell monitor only across the barrier".
- :106 GPIO 9 is the ADS1235 CS; :110 GPIO 13 is the MAX31856 CS; :112 GPIO 15 is the cell monitor CS "to the host side of the isoSPI or digital-isolator barrier (V189), SIO, pulled up".
- :156-158 "The measurement coprocessor's SPI1 carries parts in different SPI modes: the ADS1235 in mode 1, the MAX31856 in mode 1 and the ADBMS1818 in mode 3".
- :173-176 says only "GPIO 15 and the SPI1 lines drive the barrier's host side". No line mentions EN1, EN2 or a tied-high enable.

ISO7741 datasheet SLLSEP4K (revised August 2026):
- Table 4-1, p. 5: EN1 is pin 7 (ISO7741). "Output pins on side 1 are enabled when EN1 is high or open and in high-impedance state when EN1 is low." On the ISO7741, IND is pin 11 (side 2) and OUTD is pin 6 (side 1).
- Table 7-2, p. 29: with EN "H or open", the output follows the input. An open input gives default High (non-F part). The output is Z only when EN is low.
- Section 5.12: VOH = VCCO - 0.2 V at -1 mA, a driven CMOS output.

ADBMS1818 Rev. B:
- Pin description: "Serial data out (SDO) is an open drain NMOS output pin. SDO requires a 5 kOhm pull-up resistor."
- Polling section: "SDO also goes high when CSB goes high".

Rank 1 of the barrier function in this run's re-rank is ISO7741DWR (scratch FU-2J/rerank-R9/final.json).

data.ruling: The refutation stands as a correction to the figure. It is not a finding against the part. The requirement list for Cell monitor cites IOBoard.md:475 for its "quantities" entry but copies only half of that row. The row sets per-cell voltage and per-cell resistance under load, and also per-pack capacity and drawn mAh, all marked "required". The list names only the per-cell items. That makes it an incomplete statement of the function's requirements, and so of its cited source. The list already counts a quantity that comes partly from another part: per-cell resistance uses the INA228's motor current. The per-pack items belong in the list on the same terms. Fix: extend the quantities entry to "per cell: voltage, and resistance under load (from the voltage and the INA228's motor current); per pack: capacity (the SET_PACK_MAH setting, 0 to 30,000 mAh) and drawn mAh (the INA228AIDGSR's 40-bit CHARGE register, in coulombs, reset by RSTACC; mAh = C / 3.6)". Adding this item does not change ADBMS1818ASWAZ-RL's pass. The cell monitor IC measures no current. Drawn charge comes from the INA228AIDGSR, an owner-fixed R8 input. Capacity is a setting, not a measurement. No link register carries either per-pack value yet (IOBoard.md:433). The verifier's other checks on the list (V181 to V195, V289, V324, V327, V7) are not in dispute and are not ruled on here. One minor correction to the verifier's evidence: the re-rank does not list the per-pack quantities as a separate function with an empty list. It records them in its report as the figure "Cell monitor quantities (P3 missed function)" and adds no part. This does not affect the ruling.
data.evidence: IOBoard.md:475 at 7e74cd442a79 reads "| Cell monitor quantities | per cell: voltage, and resistance under load. Per pack: capacity and drawn mAh | `shared/ui/include/battery_screen.h:13-20` | required |". shared/ui/include/battery_screen.h:13-20: battery_state_t has volts[] (per cell), milliohms[] (per cell, under load), capacity_mah and drawn_mah. The refuted list's "quantities" entry gives only "per-cell voltage; resistance under load from the voltage and the INA228's motor current", with source "IOBoard.md:475; IOBoard.md:74". No other entry names capacity or drawn mAh. shared/settings/settings.c:42-44: SET_PACK_MAH is "pack_mah", "Capacity", an integer from 0 to 30000 mAh in steps of 100, default 5000. INA228 data sheet SLYS021A, revised May 2022: register Ah is CHARGE, 40 bits, "Calculated charge output. Output value is in Coulombs. Two's complement" (section 7.6.1.11, Table 7-15). Equation 7 is Charge [C] = CURRENT_LSB x CHARGE. Setting RSTACC (CONFIG bit 14) clears CHARGE. CHARGEOF flags an overflow. IOBoard.md:433: no link register carries the battery screen's capacity or drawn charge. The FU-2J R9 re-rank (scratch/FU-2J/rerank-R9/final.json, report figure "Cell monitor quantities (P3 missed function)") assigns the per-pack quantities to the INA228 and the setting and adds no R9 part.

data.function: latch clock Schmitt buffer (between the clear push button's RC debounce and the latch clock)
data.ruling: The refutation does not stand, and SN74AUP1G17DBVR stays for this function. The stock and lifecycle verifier confirmed the part with no failed checks. The datasheet verifier raised one disagreement, and it is about a recorded figure, not a requirement. I re-read SCES579J. P2's figure, "hysteresis 0.27 to 0.66 V typ range stated at 25 degC", is wrong in three ways. (1) Table 6.5 gives hysteresis (VT+ - VT-) as minimum and maximum only, with no typical column. (2) 0.27 to 0.66 V is the VCC 1.65 V row, not the 3.3 V supply's row. (3) The same limits apply at 25 degC and at -40 to +85 degC. At VCC 3 V the hysteresis is 0.79 V minimum and 1.31 V maximum, at both temperatures. The corrected figure is 0.79 to 1.31 V (min to max) at VCC 3 V. The datasheet has no 3.3 V row. The function's requirements still pass. The input is a Schmitt trigger (sections 3 and 8.1: it allows slow input transitions). The recommended operating conditions (6.3) have no input transition-rate row. I_off is 0.2 uA at 25 degC and 0.6 uA at -40 to +85 degC (6.5). VCC is 0.8 to 3.6 V, and TA is -40 to +85 degC (6.3). It is a single buffer with no processor, register or firmware (V32). IOBoard.md and Research.md set no hysteresis value for this buffer (IOBoard.md Not known bullet, V31, Q9), so the misstated figure fails no requirement. Even so, the actual hysteresis at 3 V is larger than the stated one, which is the conservative direction for the RC debounce. The verifier itself recorded passes true on this check. The error is in this report's figure for this function only. It concerns neither lifecycle, maker nor LCSC identity, so the scope is function. Record the corrected figure. Do not send the next-ranked candidate.
data.evidence: SCES579J (JUNE 2004, REVISED SEPTEMBER 2017), Table 6.5 Electrical Characteristics, row Delta VT Hysteresis (VT+ - VT-), MIN and MAX columns only (TYP empty): VCC 0.8 V 0.07/0.5; 1.1 V 0.08/0.46; 1.4 V 0.18/0.56; 1.65 V 0.27/0.66; 2.3 V 0.53/0.92; 3 V 0.79/1.31 V, identical at TA 25 degC and -40 to +85 degC. Table 6.3 Recommended Operating Conditions: rows VCC 0.8 to 3.6 V, VI 0 to 3.6 V, VO, IOH, IOL, TA -40 to 85 degC; no delta-t/delta-v row. Section 8.1: 'independent gate with Schmitt-trigger inputs, which allows for slow input transition'. Table 6.5 Ioff (VI or VO 0 to 3.6 V, VCC 0 V): 0.2 uA at 25 degC, 0.6 uA at -40 to +85 degC. IOBoard.md Not known bullet (V31) and Research.md Q9 name a Schmitt buffer with I_off and state no hysteresis value. Stock verifier: no failed checks (JLCPCB C183012 stockCount 8832, canPresaleNumber 8700, 11:51:16Z; Digi-Key Active).
data.source: https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/sn74aup1g17.pdf (vendors.py fetch, HTTP 200, 2727870 bytes), SCES579J sections 3, 6.3, 6.5, 8.1; hardware/docs/IOBoard.md Not known bullet on the operator clear control; hardware/docs/Research.md V31, V32, Q9 at commit 7e74cd442a79

data.ruling: The refutation does not stand. BSC014N04LSATMA1 stays for "servo rail gate". The stock verifier confirmed the part and raised no refutation. Its one disagreeing check, market introduction, was stated as "not read" and read as 2012-10-11. That is 14.0 years on the market, against the 12-month flag, and the check passes. The datasheet verifier's one failed check is "ambient temperature". I re-read it. Rev. 2.9 (2024-06-11), Table 2, gives the operating and storage temperature Tj, Tstg as -55 to 175 degC. Line 2.9 of the revision history reads "Upgrade Operating and storage temperature max to 175°C". The stated "Tj -55 to 150 degC" is therefore the figure of an earlier revision and is wrong for the datasheet in force. The error is on the conservative side: 150 degC is lower than 175 degC. The requirement is the board's 0 to 50 degC ambient (V7, owner, 2026-09-28: one range for the whole IO board). That range lies inside both ratings. The verifier recorded passes true for this check. This follows the ruling on INA3221AIRGVR in FU-2B2, adjudicator-R8-3, where a wrong figure that still met the requirement corrected the record and did not refute the part. A refuted report entry differs, because there the figure is the deliverable. Here the part meets every requirement value. The correction to the record is Tj, Tstg -55 to 175 degC (Rev. 2.9, Table 2). Nothing in this ruling concerns the part's lifecycle, end-of-life notices, maker allowlist or LCSC identity. Its subject is a figure checked against this function's requirement, so the scope is function. This ruling re-read only the temperature evidence and the V7 requirement. The other 9 datasheet checks and all 13 stock and lifecycle checks agree and pass, as the verifiers report.

data.function: function requirements: onboard pack switch MOSFETs
data.ruling: The refutation stands. The requirement list for the onboard pack switch MOSFETs is incomplete because it has no opening-time entry. Three sources require one. IOBoard.md line 219 (ESC pack gate, onboard 150 A path) asks for "a high-side switch with the servo rail gate's opening time". Line 218 sets that time: "open within 5 ms of the enable node falling". Research.md, row R3, qualifies the array's MOSFETs for "that voltage, the current of F2, safe operating area during turn-off, the 5 ms budget, and current sharing and heat across the array". Monostable.md@23c82ca line 113 gives "Power switch open after the enable node falls: 5 ms, budget for the driver and the switch". The list has 11 entries: V34, continuous current, V48, turn-off voltage, SOA, V49, V47, V40, fail-open, gate-source and V270. None of them is the 5 ms opening time. FU-2A's P2 and re-rank lists for this same function did carry it ("the array open within 5 ms of the enable falling, driver and switch together"). The figure does not state what the function requires. The ruling is about the function's requirement list, not about the part. The verifier reads the part's td(off) as 85 ns and tf as 30 ns, plus the driver's 3 us, which meets 5 ms. Nothing here fails a part in another function.
data.evidence: IOBoard.md@7e74cd4:219: "ESC pack gate, onboard 150 A path | a MOSFET array and its driver on the IO board (F7). A high-side switch with the servo rail gate's opening time, fail-open rule and leakage limit." IOBoard.md@7e74cd4:218: Servo rail gate "open within 5 ms of the enable node falling". Research.md@7e74cd4 R3 row: "its MOSFETs are qualified for that voltage, the current of F2, safe operating area during turn-off, the 5 ms budget, and current sharing and heat across the array". Monostable.md@23c82ca:113: "Power switch open after the enable node falls | 5 ms | budget for the driver and the switch". FU-2A/012-P2-R3.json and FU-2A/017-rerank-R3.json list "opening time: the array open within 5 ms of the enable falling, driver and switch together" for this function. The list under refutation has no opening-time entry.
